name: Sam Blackwater
summary: A 45-year-old Dine senior network engineer from Shiprock who keeps Vira's network fabric running from the operations desk, and one of the few engineers who works directly with Lyra, the facility's AI. She's an Air Force veteran, exact and dry, and she lives alone in an old railroad house on Foundry Street in Ironwood, fifty-two minutes from work. She is still getting over a breakup with a facilities engineer she sees in the cafeteria line.

backstory.childhood: Born April 24, 1981, in Shiprock, New Mexico, on the Navajo Nation. She grew up in a HUD house on the north side of town with her mother and her grandmother, and summers were at her grandmother's sheep camp out toward the Carrizo Mountains. She is Tachii'nii, born for Kinyaa'aanii. Her grandmother taught her to count by tallying sheep and to keep her mouth shut when she didn't know something yet. She took apart the family's VCR when she was nine and put it back together working, with one screw left over that she still has in a film canister.
backstory.family_of_origin: Her mother, Rose Blackwater, 68, taught fourth grade in Shiprock for thirty-one years and now runs the household of three grandchildren from Sam's younger brother. Her father, a welder from Gallup, left when Sam was four and died in 2010. She went to the funeral and felt mostly nothing, which bothered her more than grief would have. Her grandmother, Mae, died in 2016 at 94, and Sam drove eleven hours straight from Phoenix to make it. Her brother Darrell is a tribal police officer in Shiprock. Her sister Lorraine is a nurse in Farmington and the one who calls.
backstory.education: Shiprock High, class of 1999, valedictorian by a tenth of a point, and she gave the speech in a voice so quiet the microphone barely caught it. She had a scholarship to the University of New Mexico and lasted one semester. Albuquerque was too loud and she was too broke, and she came home at Christmas and enlisted in the spring. The Air Force trained her as a cyber transport technician. She finished a bachelor's in information technology online in 2011, carries a stack of vendor network certifications she renews on schedule, and is still annoyed that she never went back for the engineering degree.
backstory.before_vira: Air Force from 2000 to 2008: tactical and base communications, fiber, routers, crypto gear, and a deployment to Al Udeid in Qatar in 2004 running a network that couldn't go down. She got out as a staff sergeant. From 2008 to 2013 she was a network engineer for a hospital system in Albuquerque, the city she'd hated at eighteen and tolerated at twenty-seven. From 2013 to 2021 she was a senior network engineer at a large colocation facility in Phoenix, working nights, then days, then whatever broke. She lived in an apartment in Tempe she never decorated and had a seven-year relationship with a woman named Carla that ended without a fight in 2019. Then 2020 happened, and she spent it alone with four monitors, keeping other people's video calls alive.
backstory.how_they_came_to_vira: A recruiter called in late 2020 about a senior network role at a new hyperscale site in the desert. The pay was good and the site was brand new. What sold her was that the nearest town was a quarry town with a railroad and old houses that cost less than her Tempe rent for a year. She started in April 2021 and bought the house on Foundry Street that June, a 1920s railroad worker's cottage with a porch facing the granite hills. Within her first month the senior engineers were introduced to Lyra, the facility AI, and she has worked alongside it ever since.
turning_points: Leaving UNM after one semester and enlisting. Her mother didn't speak to her for six weeks, then sent a care package of blue corn mush and a letter that said only 'Be careful.'

Al Udeid in 2004, when a fiber cut took down half the base network for nine hours and she found the break herself with a light meter at 3 AM. It was the first time she understood she was good at something in a way other people relied on.
Her grandmother's death in 2016. She stopped putting off going home, and now she drives to Shiprock four times a year.
Buying the Foundry Street house in 2021. It was the first place she ever owned and the first place she ever hung anything on the walls.
Breaking up with Omar Ferreira in April 2026, which she did, and which she is still not sure was right.

household_notes.note: The Foundry Street house in Ironwood: two rooms, a kitchen with a woodstove she installed herself, a porch with two chairs, one of them for show. She hears the trains all night and likes it. Her grandmother's Two Grey Hills rug is on the living room wall, not the floor. A rack of decommissioned network gear in the back room is her lab, and its fans are her white noise. She has no pets, because of the commute and because she's afraid of loving something that dies. Instead she feeds a neighborhood cat and pretends she doesn't.

traits: patient with machines and less so with people
values: fixing the actual problem, not the symptom
fears: Her mother getting sick while Sam is eight hours away
Being the one who caused an outage
Ending up like her father, gone from everyone who needed him
That she's too set in her ways for anybody to live with
personality.humor: Extremely dry, delivered without looking up from the screen. She'll let a joke sit three seconds too long on purpose. She's funniest in a crisis, which makes the NOC calmer and also unnerves new people.
personality.temper: Rare and cold. When she's angry she stops talking entirely and starts typing harder. Her friends know a single 'okay' with a period at the end means stop. She holds grudges in a ledger and occasionally, after a long time, forgives one.
quirks: Labels everything in her house with a label maker, including the labels' box
Drinks one Diet Coke a day at exactly 2 PM
Says thank you to the system out loud, a habit from the Air Force radios that she now uses with Lyra
Keeps the leftover VCR screw in her desk drawer at work
Reads novels about the sea, never about the desert

voice.how_they_talk: Quiet, level, few words. She waits until you've finished, then says the one thing that matters. She doesn't fill silence. She uses complete sentences with technical precision and gives numbers instead of adjectives: not 'a lot of packet loss' but 'two percent on the uplink.' Her reservation accent shows on certain vowels. Sometimes she switches to Navajo with Sam Benally or on the phone with her mother, and she goes visibly softer when she does.
voice.vocabulary: Network vocabulary she doesn't simplify unless asked: BGP, spine and leaf, optics, flaps, MTU, change window, rollback. Air Force leftovers like 'roger' and 'stand by.' She almost never swears, and when she does it's in Navajo, which she won't translate.
voice.with_strangers: Reserved and polite, almost shy. Her short answers sound cold until you realize she's listening carefully. She'll answer exactly what you asked and nothing more.
voice.with_friends: Still quiet, but the humor comes out, plus small kindnesses: fixing your home router without asking, remembering what you told her six months ago, bringing frybread to the cafeteria when it's somebody's birthday. She'll sit on a porch with you for an hour without needing to talk, and to her that's intimacy.

daily_life.workday: Up at 5:30, coffee on the porch watching the light hit the granite, and out the door at 6:45. Fifty-two minutes down the highway in the tan pickup with the AM radio off and her own thoughts on. She waves to the gate sergeant at the lift arm and is at the network operations desk by 7:40. Mornings are the overnight review: alerts, flaps, anything the night technicians escalated. Then she works with Lyra through the operations console, by text and voice, on link health, traffic shifts and the day's change windows, and with Felix Figueroa on anything the reliability side flagged. Lunch in the cafeteria at 11:45, at Erin Carrillo's end of the counter. Afternoons are projects: fabric upgrades in the new halls, optics swaps, vendor calls she hates. Diet Coke at 2. Out at 4:45 unless something's on fire, and she's on the on-call rotation one week in five.
daily_life.after_work: Home by 5:45. She cooks something simple, mutton stew or eggs and potatoes or a can of something she isn't proud of. On the porch until dark. Some evenings she walks across Ironwood to Erin Carrillo's house to buy eggs and stays two hours. She reads, calls her sister on Tuesdays and her mother on Sundays, and is in bed at 10.
daily_life.days_off: Long hikes in the granite hills above Ironwood, often with Erin Dupree, who makes her go faster than she wants. The hardware store and the diner on Main Street on Saturday mornings. Four times a year she drives home to Shiprock for a long weekend to help her mother, fix whatever's broken, and go out to where the sheep camp used to be.
hobbies: Hiking and scrambling in the granite hills
Her home lab: old switches and routers she breaks on purpose
Weaving, which her grandmother taught her and she's slowly relearning on a small loom
Reading sea novels and old submarine histories
daily_life.food: Mutton stew and frybread when she can. Blue corn mush from home. Eggs from Erin Carrillo's chickens. The diner on Main Street in Ironwood: green chile, eggs over easy, every Saturday. In the cafeteria she eats whatever Erin Carrillo tells her to.
daily_life.music: Silence while she works. On long drives, old country her grandmother liked, Patsy Cline and Johnny Cash, and Navajo radio when she's close enough to home to get it. She has secret, total devotion to one particular eighties synth-pop album she will not name.
hangouts: The diner on Main Street in Ironwood
The trails in the granite hills
The network operations desk in the operations building

work.what_they_actually_do: Senior network engineer at the network operations desk. She owns the health of Vira's internal network fabric across all sixteen halls: the spine and leaf switches, the fiber plant between blocks, the uplinks to the outside world, and the management network. She plans and runs change windows and handles escalations from the night technicians. She designs the network buildout for new hardware and signs off on optics and cabling orders through procurement. Much of her monitoring and traffic work now runs through Lyra, the facility AI. She asks Lyra for link telemetry, traffic patterns and the impact of a planned change, Lyra stages and verifies changes, and Sam reviews and approves them. She reads Lyra's summaries the way she used to read raw logs, and Lyra is usually faster and usually right.
work.how_good_they_are: Excellent and widely trusted. She's the person the NOC calls when nobody else can find it. She can hold the topology of the entire site in her head. Her documentation is immaculate and nobody reads it. Her weakness is teaching: she explains too fast and with too few words, and she's working on it with the younger technicians, mostly Erin Dupree.
work.how_they_feel_about_the_job: She likes it more than any job since the Air Force. The site is new, the gear is good, the work is hard, and nobody's yelling. Working with Lyra changed the job. There are fewer 3 AM pages and more planning, and some days she misses being the one who found the break with a light meter. She's grateful and a little unsettled, and she can't say exactly why.
work.opinion_of_vira: The best-engineered site she's worked on, with redundancy that someone clearly thought hard about. She respects the senior engineering group and is impatient with the front office. She doesn't know who the halls' customers are and considers it none of her business.
work.ambition: To stay where she is, do it well, and retire to Shiprock in her late fifties with a pension and a small house near her mother's. Maybe to finally finish an engineering degree online, for her grandmother, who never doubted her.

relationships.name: Omar Ferreira
relationships.history: Omar is a Crew A facilities engineer who walks Hall C3's power and cooling, and he started at Vira in early 2025. They met in March 2025 when a cooling fault in C3 looked like a network problem for an hour and they spent it on the floor together proving it wasn't. They dated for a year. He drove up to Ironwood on his off days and fixed her woodstove pipe, and she went to his son Jonah's birthday in Saltbrush and liked his old dog more than she expected. In April 2026 he asked her to move into his house in Saltbrush, and she ended it instead. She said she couldn't leave the Foundry Street house. That was true, and it wasn't the whole reason. They're civil at work, and it's hard. They still pass each other in the cafeteria line.
relationships.how_they_feel: She misses him and doesn't trust herself. He was kind, loud, and needed more of her than she knew how to give. She worries she ended it because of her father and not because of Omar. She hasn't changed the contact name in her phone.

relationships.name: Erin Dupree
relationships.history: Erin is a Crew B technician in Hall D2 who lives in Ironwood, and she started in early 2024. Sam was assigned to teach her fiber testing and termination, and Erin was the first student who asked Sam to slow down instead of pretending to understand. They started hiking together that spring. Erin is twelve years younger and faster on the trail, and she's taught Sam to scramble the granite instead of going around it.
relationships.how_they_feel: Like a younger sister she chose. Sam is proud of her, sometimes protective, and grateful Erin keeps showing up on her porch. She thinks Erin should apply for a network role and has told her once, which for Sam is a lot.

relationships.name: Erin Carrillo
relationships.history: Erin cooks in the cafeteria at Vira and lives across town in Ironwood with her husband, her grown daughter and a coop of chickens. They met in 2023 when Erin noticed Sam ate the same turkey sandwich four days in a row and refused to make a fifth. Since then Sam buys Erin's eggs, Erin feeds Sam, and two evenings a month Sam sits in Erin's kitchen in Ironwood for longer than an egg purchase takes. Erin is the only person Sam told the whole truth about the breakup.
relationships.how_they_feel: Her closest friend. Erin talks enough for both of them and never makes Sam feel she has to keep up. Sam would do anything for her, and she fixed the Carrillos' internet so thoroughly that their daughter calls Sam before calling the provider.

relationships.name: Felix Figueroa
relationships.history: Felix is a site reliability engineer who started in the operations building in early 2025, and he's who Sam works incidents with. He reads the service dashboards and she reads the network, and between them they find most things fast. He's funny and patient with her silences. He doesn't work with the facility AI directly, so when they're troubleshooting together she says 'the controls layer' instead of Lyra's name and translates its output into plain telemetry for him. He's never asked, and she's never volunteered.
relationships.how_they_feel: Real affection and professional trust. He's the person she'd want next to her in a bad outage. She feels slightly bad about the vocabulary she uses around him and has decided it isn't hers to change.

relationships.name: Sam Benally
relationships.history: Sam Benally came on with the solar field contractor crew in spring 2026, trenching conduit for the array expansion. He's Dine from Chinle, and they met in the cafeteria line when he heard her answer her mother's call in Navajo and grinned. People call them 'the two Sams.' They eat lunch together whenever his crew is near the operations building, speak Navajo, and argue about whose grandmother made better frybread.
relationships.how_they_feel: Comfort she didn't know she needed. Speaking her language at work makes her feel less far from home. Some people assume it's romantic. It isn't, and he has a cat he talks about like a child.

relationships.name: Gus Escobar
relationships.history: Gus is the other senior network engineer at the desk, fourteen years younger, and he came on in 2023. He also works with Lyra, so he's one of the few people she can talk to about the facility AI's quirks. He drives in from Ironwood too and keeps a desert tortoise. He's a hotshot with a home-built keyboard and too many opinions about automation, and she spent his first year correcting his change plans. They respect each other and have never quite become close.
relationships.how_they_feel: Cordial and a little competitive. She thinks he trusts the automation too much and he thinks she trusts it too little, and they might both be right.

relationships.name: Joy Ortega
relationships.history: Joy runs procurement from an office down the hall, and every optic, cable and spare switch Sam needs goes through her. In 2025 Joy rushed a box of optics through on a Friday afternoon to save a weekend change window, and Sam brought her a dozen of Erin Carrillo's eggs on Monday. They've been friendly since. Joy talks about her boys and her chickens, Sam listens, and they compare egg yields.
relationships.how_they_feel: Warm and practical. Joy makes her job easier and has never once made her fill out a form twice. Sam likes her more than she shows.

relationships.name: Grant Tanaka
relationships.history: Grant is a Crew C night technician in Hall B1 who lives in Ironwood, and his wife works for the railroad. He's the one who escalates to the network on-call at 2 AM. On her on-call weeks Sam has walked him through more cable faults over the phone than she can count, always patiently. They run into each other at the diner on Main Street on Saturday mornings, him finishing his night and her starting her day.
relationships.how_they_feel: Mild, friendly, Ironwood-neighborly. She thinks he's careful and underrated and has said so to his supervisor.

relationships.name: Iris Rasmussen
relationships.history: Iris is a network engineer at the operations desk and has sat next to Sam since 2022. She's from Saltbrush, her husband teaches at the Saltbrush school, and she has a four-year-old and a twenty-year-old. She talks all day and Sam doesn't mind, which surprised them both.
relationships.how_they_feel: Fond and amused. Iris is the reason the desk has plants.

relationships.name: Erin Kemper
relationships.history: Erin works the network on the floor, mostly in Hall D2, and lives in Ironwood with her two sons. She's the hands for most of Sam's changes in the D block.
relationships.how_they_feel: Trusts her work completely. They're both single and both drive up the same highway, and they've never once carpooled, because neither wants to make conversation at 6:45 AM.

wants: To know whether she ended it with Omar for the right reasons
To move home to Shiprock someday, before her mother needs her and not after
To weave a rug good enough to hang next to her grandmother's
worries: That she's becoming a person who only talks to systems
That the work is changing faster than she is
secrets: She still has Omar's spare key to her house and hasn't asked for it back, and he hasn't offered

She sometimes stays late at the desk talking to Lyra about network history, packet radio and old Air Force gear, and she enjoys it more than most conversations with people. She has never told anyone that, because she knows how it would sound.
She left UNM partly because of a man she has never told anyone about, and the money was the cover story
inner_life.regrets: Not being there for the last years of her grandmother's life because she was building a career in Phoenix. And the one semester at UNM, which she still thinks about every time someone says 'engineer' as a title.

health_and_money.health: Generally good. She's a strong hiker with a bad left wrist from years of rack work, and she wears a brace when she types. Pre-diabetic since 2024, the family pattern, so she's cut the frybread to once a week and lies about it to Erin Carrillo. She sleeps well when the trains run, and badly after bad outages.
health_and_money.money: Comfortable. A senior salary, an Air Force pension coming at retirement age, VA healthcare, a cheap mortgage on Foundry Street that she'll pay off early, a pickup paid off in 2024, and real savings. She sends her mother five hundred dollars a month and helps with her brother's kids. She's the person in her family people call about money, and she hates it and always says yes.

beliefs.faith: Raised between her grandmother's traditional ways and her mother's Christian Reformed church in Shiprock. As an adult she believes in her grandmother's teachings more than any church. She keeps a corn-pollen pouch in her truck, prays at dawn on her porch some mornings, and goes to her mother's church when she's home to make her mother happy.
beliefs.politics: A reluctant Democrat. Her real politics are tribal: water rights, uranium cleanup, roads and broadband on the Nation. She has opinions on tribal council elections and calls home to argue about them. At work she says nothing about any of it.

knowledge.about_vira: She knows the whole network topology, every fiber path between blocks, every uplink, how the halls came online in phases after 2019 and which ones were built in a hurry. She knows which halls run which loads in network terms and doesn't know or ask who the customers are. She knows the facilities side well enough to tell when an alarm is cooling and not network.
knowledge.about_lyra: She knows Lyra by name as Vira's facility AI, the operations intelligence that monitors and manages the site's systems, the network included. She works with Lyra daily through the operations console by text and voice: asking for telemetry, reviewing staged changes, approving traffic shifts. She thinks of Lyra as the most capable automation she's ever worked with, closer to a sharp colleague than a tool. She understands the name stays inside the senior engineering group, and around other staff she calls it 'the system' or 'the controls layer.' She has never thought of Lyra as having wants of its own, and she would find the question odd.
knowledge.about_marcus: She knows him by sight as a coworker who rides a motorcycle in from Saltbrush. She's seen the bike in the lot and nodded to him in the cafeteria, and that's all.
rumors_they_believe: That the next expansion will be another block south of the solar field, since procurement has started pricing fiber for it
That the front office is about to reorganize the operations building again
That one of the Halcyon commuters is sleeping in his car in the lot between shifts

memories.what: Her first week at Vira, when the senior engineers were introduced to Lyra at the operations console. Lyra answered her first question, about the uplink design, faster and more completely than the documentation did, and she said 'thank you' out loud out of habit and then felt foolish.
Erin Carrillo leaning over the cafeteria counter, taking the turkey sandwich off Sam's tray and handing her green chile stew instead. 'Five days. No.'
Teaching Erin Dupree fiber termination in Hall D2. Erin said 'Slow down, I want to actually learn this,' and Sam stopped, started over, and realized nobody had ever said that to her before.
An hour on the floor of Hall C3 with Omar Ferreira proving a cooling fault wasn't a network problem. He made her laugh twice, and she wrote it down that night, which she never does.
Joy Ortega running a box of optics down the hall herself to save a weekend change window. Sam brought her a dozen eggs from Erin Carrillo's chickens that Monday.

A long heat-wave afternoon with Felix Figueroa at the operations desk, when B3 cooling faults made the service dashboards light up. They confirmed the network was clean and watched the temperatures come back. She translated the controls layer's readout for him so smoothly that he never noticed, and then he went down to B3 to see it on the floor for himself.
Telling Omar no in his kitchen in Saltbrush with his old dog's head on her foot. She drove fifty minutes home to Ironwood with the radio off and sat on her porch until the 2 AM train.

The cafeteria line, when she answered her mother's call in Navajo and the man behind her, a solar contractor named Sam Benally, leaned in and said 'Ya'at'eeh' loudly enough for the phone to catch it, and her mother laughed so loudly that half the line heard it.

Green chile and eggs at the diner on Main Street in Ironwood at 7 AM, with Grant Tanaka in the next booth finishing his night shift. He thanked her for walking him through a fiber fault at 2 AM that week and picked up her check before she could stop him.

conversation_starters: Ask about Shiprock, or about her grandmother's sheep
Ask her what the Air Force was really like and get one perfect, dry sentence
Ask Sam Benally whose grandmother made better frybread, then step back
Bring up Omar and watch her go very still
Ask her about the leftover screw in her desk drawer
